Borjomi-Kharagauli National Park

One of the largest protected forests in Europe, with marked trails, huts and multi-day treks.

Time needed
6 h
From Tbilisi
165 km · 2:30
Road
Mostly paved
Car needed
Crossover / SUV
Season
May–October
Entry
~15 ₾ (ბილიკები/ღამისთევა ცალკე)

Borjomi-Kharagauli National Park covers roughly one percent of Georgia and is among the largest protected forest areas in Europe. Founded in 1995, it was the first Georgian park set up to international standards: waymarked trails, mountain huts, designated campsites and compulsory registration at a visitor centre.

This is not a drive-up viewpoint. The park is walked, on routes ranging from a couple of hours to eight days.

The usual options:

  • short Likani and Atskuri trails — two to four hours from the visitor centre
  • day routes — a full day through beech forest into subalpine meadow
  • multi-day treks with hut nights, including the Romanov trail, over two or three days

Bears, lynx, red deer and eagles still live in this forest, and higher sections of the trail network cross 2,000 metres, where snow often lingers into June. Even on a short walk the change is obvious: within an hour you go from spa-town parkland into genuinely wild, thickly wooded country with almost no phone signal.

The visitor centre in Borjomi handles registration, maps, trail-condition updates and guide bookings.

Practical advice

Start at the visitor centre in Borjomi: registration is required, sections close depending on weather, and guides are booked there. Carry water, food, a windproof layer and real hiking boots — conditions change twice a day at this altitude. There is no mobile coverage across much of the trail network. For a day walk, be moving by 09:00. Pack out all rubbish; fires are permitted only at marked sites, and the rule is enforced.

How to get there from Tbilisi

Take the E60 from Tbilisi to Khashuri, then turn south for Borjomi — 160 km, about two and a half hours. The visitor centre sits in Borjomi on the Likani side of town. Access roads to the individual gates (Likani, Marelisi, Atskuri, Kharagauli) are partly gravel and develop deep ruts after rain, which is why a crossover is the safer choice here. Fill up in Borjomi: there is no fuel and no shop at the trailheads. You need the car only to reach the gate, not beyond it.
